headline: Arizona's attorney general has threatened legal action against the developer of a data center in south Phoenix, citing harm to nearby residents.
score_reason: Stays at the pool score: a state official threatening a nuisance lawsuit, though no action has been filed.
importance_line: Residents near the Ahwatukee site and near the nearly 50 planned Arizona data centers are affected, but no lawsuit has been filed and the attorney general says she cannot yet say what action she will take.
summary: Courthouse News reports that Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes, a Democrat, told a town hall in Mesa on 14 Oct 2026 that she is investigating the MenLo Digital data center under construction in Ahwatukee and "has not been shy" about using public nuisance law, after residents described construction noise up to 110 decibels and dust. Mayes says nearly 50 data centers are being built or planned in Arizona and will add to energy costs and water stress, and she wants a pause on approvals that she cannot impose alone.
notes: Own reporting by Courthouse News. Mayes said she could not confirm what action or when.
